package_info.why_malicious: The script was covertly injected into the Morfix online dictionary website through a compromised advertisement network. As a result, users' browsers were forced to mine cryptocurrency without their knowledge or consent, leading to unauthorized exploitation of user CPU resources, increased power consumption, degraded device performance, and potential privacy risks.

execution_context.trigger: When a user visits the compromised website and the advertisement loads
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the website's HTML or dynamically loaded JavaScript via third-party advertisement network

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At page load, the code loads a remote CoinHive JavaScript mining library, initializes a mining client with a site key, and immediately starts mining cryptocurrency using the user's CPU; mined hashes are sent over the network to the attacker's mining pool, resulting in unauthorized resource consumption and potential profit for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code silently loads a known cryptocurrency mining library and initiates mining operations in the user's browser without any notification or consent, hijacking computational resources for the attacker's financial gain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate website scripts and advertisements should not perform intensive background computations or use the user's device for cryptocurrency mining without explicit user consent and clear disclosure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some websites may offer browser-based mining as an alternative to ads, but only after obtaining explicit user consent and providing clear notification to the user.
key_indicators: Inclusion of CoinHive or other known mining library scripts via <script src> tags
Automatic invocation of mining functions (e.g., CoinHive.Anonymous, miner.start()) on page load
No user-facing notification or opt-in mechanism for mining activity
Sustained, abnormal CPU usage in browser processes immediately after visiting the site
Outbound network connections to mining pool domains (e.g., coinhive.com)

attack_chain.action: A malicious cryptocurrency mining script is injected into the Morfix website through a compromised third-party advertisement network.
attack_chain.leads_to: The mining script is loaded into the user's browser when the advertisement is displayed.

attack_chain.action: When a user visits the website and the advertisement loads, the mining script executes in the user's browser, initializing and starting mining operations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continuous mining activity in the user's browser, hijacking CPU resources and sending mined hashes to the attacker's mining pool.

behavioral_signatures: Web pages loading known crypto-mining JavaScript libraries such as CoinHive or Crypto-Loot
JavaScript code that automatically starts mining operations (e.g., calls to CoinHive.Anonymous and miner.start()) without user interaction
Browser tabs exhibiting sustained, abnormally high CPU usage immediately after page load
file_indicators: Presence of <script src="https://coinhive.com/lib/coinhive.min.js"> or similar mining library URLs in website source code
Inline JavaScript code invoking mining-related functions such as CoinHive.Anonymous and miner.start()
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S connections to known mining pool domains (e.g., coinhive.com, cryptoloot.pro)
Frequent small POST or GET requests to mining service endpoints associated with mining pools
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web traffic for inclusion of known mining script URLs and analyze JavaScript for mining-related function calls. Use browser or endpoint monitoring to detect tabs with sustained high CPU usage after page load. Network monitoring tools should alert on outbound connections to known mining pool domains. Web application firewalls and browser security extensions can block or alert on the inclusion of mining scripts or suspicious mining-related network activity.
